name: platforms
title: Assessed platforms
citation: Whelan CD, Smith-Byrne K. Atlas of Proteomic Technologies: an evidence-based framework for selecting and combining commercial proteomics platforms. bioRxiv 2026. https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.10.750723

data.name: Olink Explore HT
data.technology: Proximity Extension Assay (PEA), dual-antibody, NGS readout
data.readoutInstruments: Illumina NovaSeq, NextSeq, or Ultima UG100
data.sampleInput: ~2 µL consumed in reaction; ~40 µL recommended to account for instrument dead volume and transfer losses
data.sampleTypes: Plasma and serum fully validated; CSF and other biofluids compatible with caveats
data.precision: Median CV ~11.4% (Explore 3072) to ~26.8% (Explore HT) per Alkahest 2025 study; CV improves significantly for proteins above LOD
data.throughput: Semi-automated, ~10M data points/week; 172 samples per reagent kit
keyLimitations: Higher proportion of HT assays below LOD in plasma versus the earlier Explore 3072 panel
data.overview: Olink Explore HT is the leading affinity-based proteomics platform for large-scale epidemiological research, using Proximity Extension Assay (PEA) technology that requires dual-antibody binding before signal generation: dramatically reducing off-target noise. With ~5,400 assays and deployment in landmark studies including the UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project (UKB-PPP, 54,000+ participants) and a Regeneron ~200K-sample initiative, it is the de facto standard for population-scale plasma proteomics. Note: although only ~2 µL is consumed in the reaction, ~40 µL is typically recommended to account for instrument dead volume, transfer losses, and potential evaporation. It is best suited for researchers who prioritize specificity and validated cis-pQTL support over raw protein count.
bestFor: Large population cohorts (>1,000 samples) in plasma or serum
Genetic association studies (GWAS/pQTL) where specificity is critical
Studies replicating findings from UKB-PPP or other Olink reference datasets
Archived biobank samples with limited volume (~40 µL recommended; ~2 µL consumed in reaction)
Consortium-scale studies where cross-lab standardization matters

considerInstead.reason: If maximizing protein coverage (9,500 vs 5,400) or data bridging to historical SomaScan datasets is a priority
If absolute quantification or cost efficiency at very high sample volumes (>5,000) is the primary driver
If MS-based pQTL discovery in a non-European ancestry cohort, or unbiased discovery without pre-specified target lists, is needed

data.name: SomaSeq
data.throughput: Automated NGS library prep on Illumina sequencers; ~9,500 proteins per sample in ~2.5 days
keyLimitations: Lower target specificity than the dual-binding affinity platforms: single-aptamer binding with documented epitope effects and matrix sensitivity
Lowest cis-pQTL support (~43%): less suited to genetics-first study designs
Documented agreement with Olink is modest: median Spearman correlation 0.33 across 1,848 matched assays (Eldjarn et al., 2023); comparable data against other platforms has not been published

Most published evidence (including pQTL and head-to-head studies) derives from the earlier array-based SomaScan readout, not the current NGS readout: performance characteristics may differ and the NGS evidence base is still emerging
data.note: Historical studies reference 'SomaScan 7K,' 'SomaScan 11K,' or 'SomaLogic': these are the same underlying aptamer (SOMAmer) technology, originally an array-based readout, now adapted to next-generation sequencing and marketed by Illumina as SomaSeq (briefly sold as Illumina Protein Prep)
data.overview: SomaSeq (Illumina), the NGS successor to the SomaScan microarray assay, briefly sold as Illumina Protein Prep, is the highest-coverage commercial proteomics platform, measuring ~9,500 unique human proteins from a single plasma or serum sample using modified DNA aptamers (SOMAmers). It offers best-in-class precision (median CV ~5.3%) and unmatched cross-version data bridging from the 5K → 7K → 11K → current platform, enabling longitudinal studies and meta-analyses across years of data. Its key limitation is specificity: single-aptamer binding carries elevated single-epitope binding-artifact risk relative to dual-binding designs, the lowest cis-pQTL support (~43%), and modest cross-platform correlation. It is well-suited for broad discovery and high-precision panel development, but should be used with caution in study designs where target confidence is critical. Following Illumina's $425M acquisition of SomaLogic in January 2026, the platform is being integrated into the Illumina NGS ecosystem.
bestFor: Discovery studies prioritizing maximum proteome breadth (9,500 proteins)
Longitudinal studies or meta-analyses requiring cross-version data bridging
High-precision biomarker panel development where CV is critical
Studies building on existing SomaScan 5K/7K/11K datasets
CLIA-certified clinical research requiring a regulated laboratory

considerInstead.reason: If specificity and cis-pQTL support are more important than coverage: Olink's dual-antibody gating reduces off-target signal significantly

If studying Alzheimer's biomarkers (p-tau217, Aβ42/40): NULISA's attomolar sensitivity and blood p-tau217 measurement (research use only), benchmarked against amyloid PET and Simoa, make it the stronger choice
If absolute quantification is required: SomaSeq provides relative quantification only

data.historicalNames: This platform has been sold under several names. Published literature may reference it as SomaScan 1.3K, SomaScan 5K, SomaScan 7K, SomaScan 11K, or simply SomaLogic. The underlying aptamer (SOMAmer) technology is the same across all versions, with expanding panels. Following Illumina's acquisition of SomaLogic (January 2026, $425M), the platform is now marketed as SomaSeq (and was briefly sold as Illumina Protein Prep). Cross-version data bridging tools are available. Readout note: Earlier SomaScan versions used a microarray (array-based) readout; SomaSeq uses an NGS readout. The majority of published studies, including most pQTL analyses and head-to-head comparisons cited in this tool, were conducted using the array-based readout. The NGS implementation is newer, and performance differences between readout methods have been reported; independent validation of the NGS readout is still accumulating.

data.name: NULISA
data.technology: Antibody-based, dual capture and release mechanism, NGS readout
data.proteins: Focused panels: Inflammation (250 targets), CNS Disease (220 targets)
data.quantification: Relative, with some absolute quantification for specific biomarkers (e.g., p-tau217)
data.sensitivity: Attomolar: limit of detection 10 aM (0.24 fg/mL) for HIV p24 in plasma (Feng et al. 2023); highest sensitivity score of any affinity platform
keyStrengths: Blood p-tau217 classified amyloid PET status with AUC 0.92 to 0.93 in two cohorts (Rea Reyes et al. 2025; Zeng et al. 2024)
CNS panel also measures ApoE4 protein (Rea Reyes et al. 2025)
Blood p-tau217 measurement comparable to Simoa (research use only)
keyLimitations: Narrow panel coverage (470 proteins across both panels)
data.note: NOT a broad proteome platform: focused on inflammation and CNS disease panels
data.overview: NULISA (Nucleic acid Linked Immuno-Sandwich Assay) by Alamar Biosciences is not a broad-proteome discovery platform; it is a precision, ultra-sensitive targeted assay purpose-built for low-abundance proteins in neurodegeneration and inflammation. Its dual capture-and-release mechanism reached a limit of detection of 10 aM (0.24 fg/mL) for HIV p24 in plasma, nearly 10-fold below Simoa (Feng et al. 2023). For Alzheimer's disease biomarker studies it offers blood p-tau217 measurement (research use only) that classified amyloid PET status with AUC 0.92 to 0.93 in two cohorts (Rea Reyes et al. 2025; Zeng et al. 2024), and its CNS panel also measures ApoE4 protein. For researchers studying AD, neuroinflammation, or any biology involving extremely low-abundance analytes, NULISA fills a niche no other platform matches.
bestFor: Alzheimer's disease and neurodegeneration biomarker studies (p-tau217, Aβ42/40, NfL)
Neuroinflammation panels requiring attomolar-level sensitivity
CSF proteomics where low sample volume and high sensitivity are both needed
Studies requiring absolute quantification of specific AD biomarkers alongside a broader panel
Studies measuring blood p-tau217 (research use only), benchmarked against amyloid PET and Simoa

considerInstead.reason: If broad discovery across 5,400 proteins is needed rather than targeted inflammation/CNS panels
If hypothesis-free proteome-wide discovery across 9,500 proteins is the study objective
If calibrated quantification (pg/mL) at about 1,000-plex (vendor figure), with high throughput and lower cost, is needed

data.name: nELISA / Omni 1000
data.technology: Miniaturized bead-based sandwich ELISA, DNA-linked antibody pairs, flow cytometry readout
data.proteins: 1,058 proteins (Omni 1000, v2.1 marker list); also ~300-plex focused panels and custom Flex panels
data.sampleTypes: Plasma, serum, cell culture supernatants; CSF and tissue validation status TBD
data.quantification: ELISA-calibrated absolute quantification (pg/mL via recombinant standard curves): the only high-plex affinity platform reporting physical concentration units rather than arbitrary normalized units
data.sensitivity: Limits of detection down to 0.1 pg/mL; quantification across seven orders of magnitude (Dagher et al. 2025)
data.specificity: Antibody pairs preassembled on barcoded beads; in spike-in testing of a 191-plex panel, 5 of more than 36,000 possible noncognate interactions were detected (Dagher et al. 2025)
data.throughput: 1,536 wells per day on one cytometer in 384-well format; 7,392 samples on a 191-plex panel in under one week (Dagher et al. 2025)
keyStrengths: High throughput (1,536 wells per day on one cytometer)
Nature Methods (nELISA, 2025) and Nature Nanotechnology (bead barcoding, 2018) publications
keyLimitations: Newer platform with limited published head-to-head data
data.overview: Nomic Bio's nELISA / Omni 1000 is a newer entrant in high-plex proteomics: a miniaturized bead-based sandwich ELISA platform that reports ELISA-calibrated concentrations (pg/mL via recombinant standard curves). The only peer-reviewed nELISA study (Dagher et al. 2025, Nature Methods) used a 191-plex inflammation panel in cell culture samples, profiling 7,392 samples in under one week; the roughly 1,000-protein Omni 1000 panel, its use in plasma and serum, and the ~$50 per-sample price are vendor figures. Antibody pairs are preassembled on barcoded beads before signal generation, and spike-in testing of the 191-plex panel detected 5 of more than 36,000 possible noncognate interactions. It is the only high-plex affinity platform reporting physical concentration units rather than arbitrary normalized units such as NPX or RFU, though concentrations are calibration-curve-derived rather than MS-traceable. If the vendor's price and performance hold in plasma at scale, it would change what is feasible in large studies.
bestFor: Very large sample volumes (>5,000 samples) where cost efficiency is the primary constraint
Studies requiring calibrated protein concentrations (pg/mL) rather than relative normalized units
Cell culture supernatant or in vitro biology where ELISA-grade specificity is expected
Screening phases of drug development where cost per datapoint must be minimized
Biomarker validation at population scale after discovery on a broader platform

considerInstead.reason: If coverage beyond 1,000 proteins is needed, or if established cis-pQTL reference data is important
If unbiased discovery across 9,500 proteins is the goal, or cross-version data bridging to historical datasets is required
If ultra-low-abundance AD or neuroinflammation biomarkers (p-tau217, Aβ42/40) are the primary analytes

data.historicalNames: The platform technology is called nELISA (nucleo-ELISA). The commercial product panel is called Omni 1000. Custom panels are offered as 'Flex' panels. Nomic Bio is the company name. Note: 'Nomic' is unrelated to Illumina's NovaSeq branding.

data.name: Proteograph XT
data.proteins: 10,698 protein groups (Seer PDC, April 2026); 8,079 detected at least once and 5,768 in ≥70% of samples (Pietzner et al., Nature Genetics 2026)
data.sampleTypes: Plasma, serum; strong for tissue proteomics
data.quantification: Label-free relative (MS intensity); absolute quantification possible with SIS peptides
keyStrengths: Unbiased discovery (not limited to pre-selected targets)
Can detect protein-altering variants and help resolve epitope effects (Suhre et al. 2025)
Potential for pQTL discovery in non-European ancestries (Pietzner et al. 2026)
keyLimitations: Not a turnkey service like affinity platforms
data.overview: Seer's Proteograph XT is a mass spectrometry-based platform that uses engineered nanoparticles to deplete abundant proteins and enrich the plasma proteome before LC-MS/MS data-independent acquisition (DIA) analysis. Because nanoparticles bind proteins based on physicochemical properties rather than antibody recognition, Proteograph is truly unbiased: it can detect proteins, isoforms, PTMs, and protein-altering variants that no pre-specified assay list would capture. Seer's full identification list (PDC, April 2026) confirms 10,698 protein groups, making it the broadest MS-DIA platform in this comparison. In Genes & Health, a British South Asian cohort, it showed potential for pQTL discovery in non-European ancestries (Pietzner et al. 2026); variants that differ in frequency between ancestries can also bias affinity assays through epitope effects (Nicholas et al. 2026). It is the platform of choice for researchers who need discovery without target selection bias.
bestFor: Unbiased proteome discovery without pre-specified target lists
Diverse-ancestry cohorts, where variants that alter epitope binding can bias affinity assays (Nicholas et al. 2026)
Post-translational modification (PTM) and isoform-level biology
Studies requiring peptide-level resolution or detection of protein-altering variants
Tissue proteomics alongside plasma profiling

considerInstead.reason: If turnkey service, lower CV, and stronger cis-pQTL reference data are needed without requiring MS infrastructure
If highest precision (CV ~5%) and maximum protein count in a service-lab model are prioritized
If absolute quantification and cost efficiency at large scale are more important than unbiased discovery

data.name: TrueDiscovery
data.technology: High-abundance protein depletion + MS-DIA; also offers P2 nanoparticle enrichment workflow
data.proteins: Up to 7,000 protein groups in plasma; 13,800 in tissue
data.sampleInput: ~200 µL plasma (P2 enrichment); 50 µL (NULISA targeted panels available as add-on)
data.sampleTypes: Plasma, serum, tissue, CSF, cell lysates, the broadest validated sample-type range
data.quantification: Label-free relative; absolute via SIS peptides (TrueSignature panels)
data.precision: Median CV ~29.8% (Alkahest study, older workflow); P2 enrichment claims median CVs below 10%
keyStrengths: Deepest unbiased profiling especially in tissue (13,800 proteins)
keyLimitations: Depletion step can remove proteins of interest
data.overview: Biognosys TrueDiscovery is a CRO-operated, GCP-compliant mass spectrometry platform offering the deepest unbiased proteome profiling commercially available: up to 7,000 proteins in plasma and 13,800 in tissue. It combines high-abundance protein depletion with MS-DIA, and its newer P2 nanoparticle enrichment workflow (similar in concept to Seer) achieves median CVs below 10% in plasma. Biognosys was recently acquired by Bruker, and offers an integrated discovery-to-validation pipeline (TrueDiscovery → TrueSignature). It is the strongest choice for tissue proteomics, GCP biomarker studies, or programs requiring a validated CRO with regulatory-grade documentation.
bestFor: Tissue proteomics requiring the deepest unbiased profiling (up to 13,800 proteins)
GCP-compliant biomarker studies for regulated drug development programs
Integrated discovery-to-validation workflows (TrueDiscovery → TrueSignature)
Complex sample types: CSF, cell lysates, FFPE tissue
Studies where a full-service CRO relationship is preferred over in-house capability

considerInstead.reason: If an instrument-based (rather than CRO-only) MS workflow is needed, or for pQTL discovery in non-European ancestry cohorts
If plasma-focused epidemiology with lower CV and stronger reference datasets is the priority
If CSF work is focused on AD/neuroinflammation biomarkers requiring attomolar sensitivity

data.historicalNames: Biognosys was recently acquired by Bruker (2024–2025). The TrueDiscovery brand is retained. The company also offers TrueSignature (targeted absolute quantification panels using SIS peptides) and has a partnership with Alamar Biosciences for combined NULISA + TrueDiscovery workflows.
